mainTopic: Bird species and names: the תסיל, the צוצייני doves and names with an added description (שם לווי), and a series of rulings on kosher, forbidden, and doubtful grasshoppers and birds.
overview: The גמרא first asks why a משנה about מי חטאת names only the יונה as an exception and not the תסיל. רבי זירא answers that the תסיל spits water back and the יונה does not. Next, רב יהודה rules that the צוצייני doves may be brought on the מזבח. A משנה about אזוב seems to disqualify anything with an added name, and אביי and רבא each answer this. Then come rulings on which grasshoppers and birds are kosher, many with memory signs. רב אסי lists eight doubtful birds whose gizzard peels only with a knife, and the גמרא contrasts them with a duck whose gizzard peeled by hand after softening in the sun. Later rulings deal with the swamp rooster and swamp hen, the מרדו, and birds named after wicked people or wine. שמואל's last ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why doesn't the משנה list the תסיל next to the pigeon?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה that says all birds disqualify מי חטאת except the יונה. It then asks why the תסיל is not listed too, if it is really a kind of יונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds disqualify the purification water, except for the pigeon, because it sips. But if the תסיל is a kind of pigeon, the משנה should say: except for the pigeon and the תסיל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier idea that the תסיל is a type of יונה. It points out that a משנה lists only the יונה as an exception and leaves out the תסיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that when a bird drinks from מי חטאת, water falls back from its mouth and disqualifies the rest. The יונה is the exception because it sips neatly. If the תסיל is a kind of יונה, it should share that exception, so the משנה should have named it too.

keyTerms.meaning: Purification water, made with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
It sips (sucks the water in neatly)
A bird earlier said to be a kind of יונה
But if it is so (introduces a challenge)

phrases.notes: The subject is 'all birds,' from the start of the משנה just before this line.
He means: if the תסיל really is a kind of יונה, as was said earlier.

phrases.english: let it teach: except for the pigeon and the tasil!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא לִיתְנֵי חוּץ מִיּוֹנָה וְתָסִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the תסיל as a kind of יונה by bringing a challenge from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תסיל is a type of יונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תסיל were a kind of יונה, it would sip like one, and the משנה would have listed it next to the יונה as an exception.

steps.title: The תסיל sips but spits some back
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that both birds sip. The תסיל spits some water back, so it disqualifies the water. The יונה does not spit any back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: This one sips and spits back, and that one sips and does not spit back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends the idea that the תסיל is a kind of יונה. He explains that it was left out of the משנה because it drinks a little differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being the same kind of bird does not mean having the same drinking habit. The תסיל sips like a יונה but then spits some water back into the container, and that disqualifies the מי חטאת. So the משנה was right to name only the יונה.

keyTerms.meaning: This one... and that one (a comparison of two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: The תסיל can still be a kind of יונה. It is left out of the exception only because it spits water back.
steps.confusionAlert: 'This one' (זה) in the first half is the תסיל, which spits. 'That one' in the second half is the יונה, which does not.

phrases.english: this one sips and spits back,
and that one sips and does not spit back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: זֶה מוֹצֵץ וּמֵקִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the cases: same kind of bird, different behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the תסיל is a kind of יונה, it should share the יונה's exception.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תסיל spits water back, so it disqualifies the מי חטאת even though it is a kind of יונה.

steps.title: The צוצייני doves may be sacrificed
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the doves called כופשני צוצייני may be brought on the מזבח. He says they are the same as the תורין של רחבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: These כופשני צוצייני doves are fit for the מזבח, and they are the תורין של רחבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב יהודה: a certain kind of dove counts as kosher תורין for a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah allows תורים (turtledoves) as bird offerings. רב יהודה says these specially named doves count as real תורים, and he identifies them with the תורין של רחבה. This ruling sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to be offered on the מזבח
A kind of dove with an extra name added
Turtledoves, one of the birds allowed for קרבנות
The doves of רחבה, mentioned earlier

phrases.english: and they are the very doves of Reḥava.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הָנֵי כּוּפְשָׁנֵי צוּצְיָינֵי כְּשֵׁרִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about doves fit for קרבנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כופשני צוצייני doves are kosher תורין for the מזבח.

steps.title: Challenge: a name with an added description is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about אזוב: only plain אזוב is valid, and any אזוב with an extra description in its name is not. So doves with an extra name should not be valid either.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'Hyssop,' and not Greek hyssop, not stibium hyssop, not Roman hyssop, not desert hyssop, and not any hyssop that has an added name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה from a משנה about the אזוב used to purify a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that when the Torah says 'אזוב,' it means only the plain kind, not any type with a description attached to its name. By the same reasoning, 'צוצייני doves' have an added name, so they should not count as the תורים of the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, a plant used in purification
An added name, a description attached to the main name
Greek hyssop, an example of a name with an added description

phrases.notes: From משנה נגעים 14:6. The גמרא leaves it to us to apply this to the doves.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא כׇּל אֵזוֹב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם לְוַוי.
phrases.english: and not any hyssop that has an added name.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: אֵזוֹב, וְלֹא אֵזוֹב יוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that צוצייני doves are fit for the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anything whose name carries an added description is excluded from the plain Torah term. The doves have such a name, so they should be invalid.

steps.title: אביי: only names changed before מתן תורה count
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that an added name disqualifies only if the name existed before מתן תורה and the Torah was careful about it. These doves got their extra name only later.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Anything whose name was changed before the giving of the Torah, and the Torah was particular about it, is unfit if it has an added name. But the name of these doves was not changed before the giving of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by narrowing the rule about added names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Torah said 'אזוב,' those other types were already called by different names, so the Torah's plain word left them out on purpose. The extra name 'צוצייני' came only after מתן תורה, so the Torah's word 'תורים' still includes these doves.

keyTerms.meaning: Its name was changed or modified
The Torah was particular, careful about it

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנָּה שְׁמוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: anything whose name was changed before the giving of the Torah,
and the Torah was particular about it,
if it has an added name, it is unfit.
But these, their name was not changed
before the giving of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּנָּה שְׁמוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule about added names
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any added name, at any time, excludes something from the Torah's term.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only names already changed before מתן תורה are excluded, so the later-named doves are still valid.

steps.title: רבא: locally they are just called doves
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: where these doves live, people just call them plain doves, so their name has no real added description.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These כופשני צוצייני doves, in their own place, are called simply by the plain name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second answer to the challenge from אזוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not need אביי's rule about timing. In their home area these birds carry no extra label at all, so they are not 'something with an added name.' The added name is only used by outsiders.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why צוצייני doves are kosher despite their added name: אביי says the name came after מתן תורה, and רבא says locally they are just called doves.

phrases.english: in their own place, they call them by the plain name.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָנֵי כּוּפְשָׁנֵי צוּצְיָינֵי, בְּאַתְרַיְיהוּ סְתָמָא קָרֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 4, different from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies that the case fits the rule: there is no true added name
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doves have an added name, like the excluded kinds of אזוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: In their home area they have no added name, so the rule does not apply.

steps.title: Grasshoppers from shrubs are kosher, from cabbages are not
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that grasshoppers found among shrubs are permitted, but those found among cabbages are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: These grasshoppers from among the shrubs are permitted, and those from among the cabbages are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new ruling of רב יהודה about which grasshoppers may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה identifies two kinds of grasshoppers by where they are found. The kind found in shrubs is a kosher kind. The kind found in cabbage patches is not kosher.

phrases.english: these grasshoppers from among the shrubs are permitted,
and those from among the cabbages are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הָנֵי כְּרָזֵי דְּבֵי חִילְפֵי שָׁרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new series of rulings by רב יהודה about kosher species.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grasshoppers from shrubs are kosher; grasshoppers from cabbages are forbidden.

steps.title: Eating the forbidden grasshoppers earns lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבינא adds that someone who eats the cabbage grasshoppers gets מלקות for eating a שרץ העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: And we give lashes for them, because of the prohibition of winged swarming creatures.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds to רב יהודה's ruling by saying how serious the prohibition is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cabbage grasshoppers are not just forbidden by the Rabbis. They fall under the Torah prohibition of שרץ העוף, so eating them is punished with מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Winged swarming creatures, forbidden by the Torah

phrases.english: and we give lashes for them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the cabbage grasshoppers, the forbidden kind.

phrases.english: because of the prohibition of winged swarming creatures.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: וּמַלְקִינַן עֲלַיְיהוּ מִשּׁוּם שֶׁרֶץ הָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the level of punishment to step 7's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating the cabbage grasshoppers is a Torah prohibition punished by מלקות.

steps.title: צרדא permitted, ברדא forbidden, מרדא uncertain
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the bird צרדא is kosher, the ברדא is forbidden, with a memory trick, and the מרדא is a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: The צרדא is permitted, the ברדא is forbidden, and your memory sign is 'בר מיניה' (except for it). The מרדא is uncertain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives rulings about three birds with similar names and adds a memory sign for the forbidden one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the names sound alike, he gives a sign: ברדא sounds like 'בר מיניה,' 'except for it,' meaning eat any bird except this one. The מרדא's status is unknown, so it is left as a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird whose status is uncertain

steps.whatToRemember: צרדא is permitted, ברדא is forbidden ('בר מיניה': except for it), and מרדא is a doubt.

phrases.english: and your memory sign is 'except for it,'
phrases.notes: 'בר' sounds like ברדא. Think of it as: eat any bird except for this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: צְרָדָא – שְׁרֵי, בַּרְדָּא – אֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling of רב יהודה about kosher species, following step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צרדא is kosher, ברדא is not, and מרדא is a ספק.

steps.title: Eight birds that are a doubt
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי lists eight birds whose kosher status is uncertain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: There are eight doubtful birds: חובא, חוגא, סוגא, הרנוגא, תושלמי, מרדא, כוחילנא, and בר נפחא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי gives a list of eight birds whose kosher status we are unsure about. The מרדא from step 9 is one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 called the מרדא a doubt. Now רב אסי puts it into a bigger group of eight birds with the same doubtful status. He does not yet say why they are doubtful.

keyTerms.meaning: Doubts; cases where we cannot tell whether the bird is kosher

phrases.english: The chuva, chuga, suga, and harnuga,
tushelemi, and marda, kuchilna, and bar nappacha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: שְׁמוֹנָה סְפֵיקוֹת הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the מרדא from step 9 by listing it with seven other doubtful birds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eight specific birds have a doubtful kosher status.

steps.title: Why are these birds a doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes these eight birds doubtful.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is their doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why these birds are considered a doubt. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי gave a list with no reason. The גמרא wants to know which kosher sign is unclear for these birds.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי סְפֵיקַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רב אסי's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sign makes these eight birds doubtful?

steps.title: Their gizzard peels only with a knife
steps.stepSummary: Kosher birds' gizzards peel and non-kosher ones do not, but these peel only with a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The gizzard of kosher birds peels, and the gizzard of non-kosher birds does not peel. The gizzard of these birds peels only with a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the doubt. One of the kosher signs is a gizzard whose inner lining peels off, and these birds fall in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kosher birds have a gizzard lining that peels off, and non-kosher birds do not. These eight birds' lining comes off only with a knife. So it is unclear whether they have this kosher sign.
steps.whatToRemember: The eight doubtful birds are in the middle: their gizzard peels, but only with a knife.

phrases.english: and non-kosher ones, their gizzard does not peel,
and these, their gizzard peels with a knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹפוֹת טְהוֹרִים קוּרְקְבָנָן נִקְלָף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their gizzard peels only with a knife, so the kosher sign is unclear.

steps.title: The duck in מר שמואל's house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with a duck whose gizzard peeled after it softened in the sun.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there was a duck in מר שמואל's house whose gizzard did not peel. They put it in the sun, and once it softened, it peeled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a hard-to-peel gizzard makes a bird doubtful. It brings a case where a gizzard that would not peel did peel after softening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The duck's gizzard also would not peel at first, yet after softening it peeled, and the duck was treated as kosher. So maybe these eight birds should also count as having the sign. The challenge asks why they are only a doubt.

phrases.english: that was in the house of Mar Shmuel,
and they set it in the sun,
and once it softened, it peeled!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָהִיא בַּר אֲוָוזָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי מָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a gizzard peeled only with difficulty makes the bird doubtful.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gizzard that peeled only after softening was still enough, so these birds should also count as having the sign.

steps.title: By hand versus only with a knife
steps.stepSummary: The duck's gizzard peeled by hand after softening, but these birds need a knife even after softening.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, once it softened, it peeled by hand. Here, even after it softens, it peels only with a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are different. The duck's gizzard peeled by hand after softening, but these birds' gizzards never peel by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Softening is fine as long as the lining then comes off by hand. That counts as a real peeling gizzard. Needing a knife even after softening is what makes these eight birds a doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: Peeling by hand, even after softening, is a kosher sign. Needing a knife even after softening makes the bird a doubt.

phrases.english: There, when it softened, it peeled by hand.
it peels only with a knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, כִּי רָפֵי אִיקְּלֵיף בִּידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The duck and these birds seem the same, since neither gizzard peeled at first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The duck peeled by hand after softening, but these birds need a knife even after softening.

steps.title: The swamp rooster is the מרדו
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the swamp rooster is one of the eight doubtful birds, the מרדו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The swamp rooster is one of the eight doubts, and it is the מרדו.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי identifies one of the birds on רב אסי's list. The swamp rooster is the מרדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The names on the list were unfamiliar, so אביי links one of them to a known bird. The מרדו here is the same as the מרדא in רב אסי's list and in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Swamp rooster, a male marsh bird
And this is the same as

phrases.english: is one of the eight doubts,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תַּרְנְגוֹלָא דְּאַגְמָא חַד מִשְּׁמוֹנָה סְפֵיקוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies one bird from רב אסי's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The swamp rooster is the מרדו, one of the eight doubtful birds.

steps.title: Swamp rooster forbidden, swamp hen permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא forbids the male swamp bird and permits the female, using a memory trick from עמוני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The swamp rooster is forbidden, and the swamp hen is permitted. Your memory trick: 'An עמוני man, but not an עמונית woman.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא splits the swamp bird by male and female. The rooster is forbidden and the hen is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי spoke only about the rooster. רב פפא adds that the hen of this kind is permitted. The memory trick reminds us that, just as only the עמוני man is barred from marrying into the community and not the woman, only the male bird is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Swamp hen, the female marsh bird
An עמוני man is barred from marrying into the community, but not an עמונית woman

phrases.english: and your sign: "An Ammonite man, but not an Ammonite woman."
phrases.notes: From דברים 23:4: only a male עמוני may not marry in, just as only the male bird is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תַּרְנְגוֹלָא דְּאַגְמָא אֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling on the female of the bird that אביי identified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The swamp rooster is forbidden, but the swamp hen is permitted.

steps.title: מרימר forbids the swamp hen too
steps.stepSummary: מרימר forbids the swamp hen because it was seen clawing and eating, and identifies it as the גירותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: The swamp hen is forbidden. They saw it claw its food and eat it, and it is the גירותא.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר disagrees with רב פפא and forbids the swamp hen too. His reason is that people saw it clawing its food and eating it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clawing prey (דורס) is a clear sign of a non-kosher bird. Once the hen was seen doing this, it cannot be permitted. This goes against רב פפא, who permitted the hen.

keyTerms.meaning: It clawed its food, a sign of a non-kosher bird
גירותא, the name of a non-kosher bird

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions: רב פפא permits the swamp hen, but מרימר forbids it because it claws its food.

phrases.english: they saw it claw and eat,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ מָרִימָר: תַּרְנְגוֹלְתָּא דְּאַגְמָא אֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפא about the swamp hen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The swamp hen is forbidden because it claws its food; it is the גירותא.

steps.title: שבור אנדרפטא permitted, פירוז אנדרפטא forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב permits one bird and forbids a similar one, with a memory trick of 'פירוז the wicked'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The שבור אנדרפטא is permitted, the פירוז אנדרפטא is forbidden. Your memory trick: פירוז the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: רב rules on two similar birds. One is permitted and one is forbidden, and he gives a trick to remember which is which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two birds share the name אנדרפטא, so they are easy to confuse. The trick is that פירוז was a known wicked person, so the bird named פירוז is the forbidden one.

phrases.english: and your sign: Piruz the wicked.
phrases.notes: פירוז was a known wicked person, so the bird named for him is the forbidden one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: שַׁבּוּר אַנַדַּרְפַּטָּא – שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling on specific birds with a memory trick, like step 9 and step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שבור אנדרפטא is permitted, and the פירוז אנדרפטא is forbidden.

steps.title: בוניא permitted, פרוא forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא permits the בוניא and forbids the פרוא, with a memory trick of 'פרואה the sorcerer'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The בוניא is permitted, the פרוא is forbidden. Your memory trick: פרואה the sorcerer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא rules on two more birds. The בוניא is permitted and the פרוא is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב before him, רב הונא ties the forbidden bird to a bad person. פרואה was a known sorcerer, so the bird named פרוא is the forbidden one.
steps.whatToRemember: In each memory trick, the forbidden bird has the name of a bad person (פירוז the wicked, פרואה the sorcerer).

phrases.english: and your sign: Parva'a the sorcerer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בּוּנְיָא – שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling on a pair of birds, following the same pattern as רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בוניא is permitted, and the פרוא is forbidden.

steps.title: The reclining מרדו is permitted, the bowing מרדו is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says a מרדו that rests while it eats is permitted, but one that bows down while it eats is forbidden, and he gives the פסוק about bowing to another god as a memory trick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A מרדו bird that reclines while it eats is permitted. One that bows down while it eats is forbidden. Your memory trick is: 'You shall not bow down to another god.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new ruling about the מרדו bird, which אביי mentioned earlier. He splits it into two types based on its posture while eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, אביי counted the מרדו among the doubtful birds. Here רב פפא adds a practical way to tell two kinds apart: the bird that rests while eating is kosher, and the bird that bows its head down while eating is not. The פסוק about not bowing to another god makes it easy to remember that 'bowing' goes with 'forbidden'.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not bow down to another god (the פסוק used as the memory trick)

phrases.english: A mardu that reclines and eats is permitted,
one that bows and eats is forbidden,
and your memory trick: 'You shall not bow down to another god.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַרְדּוּ זָגֵיד וְאָכֵיל – שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement in the series of bird identifications with memory tricks; it returns to the מרדו that אביי mentioned in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מרדו that reclines while eating is kosher; one that bows while eating is not.

steps.title: The 'wine drinker' bird is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל forbids the bird called the wine drinker, and he uses the rule that כהנים who drank wine may not do the Temple service as a memory trick.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The bird called 'wine drinker' is forbidden. Your memory trick is: 'Those who drank wine are unfit for the service.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds another bird to the list. It is called the 'wine drinker', and he rules that it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The memory trick ties the bird's name to a known הלכה: a כהן who drank wine is disqualified from עבודה. Just as 'drinking wine' makes the כהן unfit, the bird named 'wine drinker' is unfit to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Wine drinker', the name of a bird

phrases.english: and your memory trick: 'Those who drank wine are unfit for the service.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שָׁתְיָא חַמְרָא – אֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another independent bird ruling in the same series, again with a memory trick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bird called 'wine drinker' is non-kosher.

steps.title: The 'wine pourer' bird is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל adds a second ruling: the bird called the wine pourer is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The bird called 'wine pourer' is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives one more ruling, about a bird with a similar wine-related name, the 'wine pourer', and forbids it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate statement from שמואל, not part of the previous memory trick. It adds a second wine-named bird to the forbidden list, and the sentence continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Wine pourer' (one who mixes or pours wine), the name of a bird

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two birds: שָׁתְיָא חַמְרָא is the 'wine drinker' and מָזְגָא חַמְרָא is the 'wine pourer'. They are two different birds in two separate statements, and both are forbidden.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מָזְגָא חַמְרָא – אֲסִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same speaker, שמואל, about another bird with a wine-related name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bird called 'wine pourer' is non-kosher.
